heads.la: PROLOGUS BEATI HIERONYMI IN LIBRUM PSALMORUM.
heads.en: THE PROLOGUE OF BLESSED JEROME ON THE BOOK OF PSALMS.
PSALM X.-- According to the Hebrews.

headnotes.en: …. Sinners, false Christians: or else therefore they do not rise again in the time to come, that they may judge, or that, being judged, they may rest in the council, that is, in the college of the just

headnotes.la: …t non judicabuntur, ut perfectissimi; alii nec judicabunt, nec judicabuntur, ut damnati infideles; alii judicabuntur et salvabuntur, ut mediocriter boni; alii judicabuntur et peribunt, ut fideles mali

headnotes.la: clauduntur. Sed e contra Dominus permanet
headnotes.en: But on the contrary the Lord remaineth

headnotes.la: est gladius quem vibrabit in secundo adventu aperte judicans, et qui modo occulte, usque ad quem aliquid valent hostis frameae, sed tunc penitus deficient
headnotes.en: is the sword which he shall brandish at the second coming, judging openly, and which now judges secretly, up to which the javelins of the enemy avail somewhat, but then they shall wholly fail

headnotes.la: [n: (CASS.)] Pluraliter, cum supra inimici singulariter dixit, quia cum plures sunt daemones, quia tamen in malitia similes sunt, quasi unum
[n: (AUG.)] Id est, et strepitus et tumultus impietatis periit: vel, cum impietas evertitur, strepitus fit, quia non venit ad summam pacem, nisi qui magno strepitu cum vitiis pugnavit
headnotes.en: …t is, both the din and the tumult of impiety hath perished: or, when impiety is overthrown, a din is made, because none comes to the highest peace but he who has fought with the vices with a great din

headnotes.la: VERS. 10.--
headnotes.en: VERS. 10.--

headnotes.la: Quantum est, eum qui judex est, esse refugium pauperi, qui nihil mundi cupit
headnotes.en: How great a thing it is, that he who is judge should be a refuge to the poor man, who desires nothing of the world

headnotes.la: VERS. 11.--
headnotes.en: VERS. 11.--

headnotes.la: …transitoriis, nihil habentibus praeter, fuit, et erit. Nam quod in illis futurum est, cum venerit, fit statim praeteritum, exspectatur cum cupiditate, amittitur cum dolore, non tenetur cum certitudine
headnotes.en: …ave nothing besides "it was" and "it will be." For what in them is to come, when it has come, straightway becomes past, it is awaited with desire, it is lost with sorrow, it is not held with certainty

headnotes.la: VERS. 12.--
headnotes.en: VERS. 12.--

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Speculatio, quae modo agitur, ut perveniamus ad pacis visionem, id est, de Sion in Jerusalem: quaelibet autem studiosa speculatio fit in errorem, nisi Dominus in ea habitet
headnotes.en: … (Ibid.)] Contemplation, which is practised now, that we may come to the vision of peace, that is, from Sion into Jerusalem: but any zealous contemplation falls into error, unless the Lord dwell in it

headnotes.la: VERS. 13.--
headnotes.en: VERS. 13.--

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Sed quasi dicant, qui missi sunt evangelizare, nemo credit nobis, et occidimur, respondit: non sine fructu, quia
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] But as if they who are sent to evangelize should say, No one believes us, and we are slain, he answered: not without fruit, because

headnotes.la: in judicio, ubi gloria occiso, poena occisori erit
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Ps 9:13 *quoniam requirens sanguinem eorum*, without *ultione*] in the judgment, where there shall be glory to the slain, punishment to the slayer

headnotes.la: …: (Ibid.)] non post oblivionem, sed post longum tempus, secundum affectum infirmorum, qui oblitum putant, quia non tam cito fit ut volunt: quibus etiam adde, imo non est oblitus ut putatis: et si dixi
headnotes.en: …a long time, according to the feeling of the weak, who think him forgetful, because it is not done so quickly as they wish: to whom also add, nay, he is not forgetful, as you think: and if I have said

headnotes.la: VERS. 14.--
headnotes.en: VERS. 14.--

headnotes.la: [n: (CASS.)] In sua persona dicit quod unusquisque petit
headnotes.en: [n: (CASS.)] In his own person he says what each one asks

headnotes.la: VERS. 15.--
headnotes.en: VERS. 15.--

headnotes.la: [n: (AUG.)] Id est ab omnibus cupiditatibus, quibus itur ad mortem: mors jam est ipsa laetitia in perfruendo cupitis; unde Apostolus
headnotes.en: [n: (AUG.)] That is, from all covetous desires, by which one goes to death: death now is that very gladness in the enjoying of things desired; whence the Apostle

headnotes.la: [n: (AUG.)] Id est ab omnibus cupiditatibus, quibus itur ad mortem: mors jam est ipsa laetitia in perfruendo cupitis; unde Apostolus: « Vidua, quae vivit
headnotes.en: [n: (AUG.)] That is, from all covetous desires, by which one goes to death: death now is that very gladness in the enjoying of things desired; whence the Apostle: « A widow that liveth
[var: Vulg. 1Tim 5:6 *Nam quae in deliciis est, vivens mortua est*, "for she that is in delights is dead while she liveth"]

headnotes.la: « Portis filiae
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. 1Tim 5:6 *Nam quae in deliciis est, vivens mortua est*, "for she that is in delights is dead while she liveth"] « In the gates of the daughter

headnotes.la: Sunt omnia optima studia, etc., *usque ad* quae nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit. [n: (CASS.)] Portae contra portas, quia hae mortis, illae vitae
headnotes.en: They are all the best pursuits, etc., *as far as* which neither eye hath seen, nor ear heard. [n: (CASS.)] Gates against gates, because these are of death, those of life

headnotes.la: VERS. 16.--
headnotes.en: VERS. 16.--

headnotes.la: [n: (AUG.)] Hucusque clamor, inde dicit Ecclesia quae affligitur, exsultabo in Jesu. [n: (CASS.)] Spe enim salva est
headnotes.en: [n: (AUG.)] Thus far the cry, thereafter the Church which is afflicted says, I will exult in Jesus. [n: (CASS.)] For by hope she is saved

headnotes.la: …: (Ibid.)] Laqueus occultus, dolosa cogitatio: Pes, animae amor, qui, si pravus est, dicitur cupiditas, si rectus, charitas. Eo enim movetur anima quasi ad locum, quo se pervenisse per amorem laetatur
headnotes.en: …ul thought: the foot is the soul's love, which, if it be crooked, is called covetousness, if right, charity. For by it the soul is moved as it were to a place, whither it rejoices to have come by love
